items.reason: hc/api/views.py:415 filters Check.objects by project__owner_id=request.project.owner_id instead of the key's project, so any key (get_checks is @authorize_read, hc/api/views.py:413) lists every project of the same owner; for a read-write key to_dict adds uuid, ping_url, update/pause/resume URLs and channels (hc/api/models.py:473-483). A rw member of one project can create its key (hc/accounts/views.py:385-392). Per-check views still compare check.project_id with request.project.id (e.g. hc/api/views.py:483, 525, 549), so other projects' per-check calls return 403. Matches ground truth P-1.

True of the code but asserts no defect: get_check, update_check, delete_check, pause, resume, pings, ping_body and flips all compare check.project_id with request.project.id (hc/api/views.py:483, 502, 525, 549, 576, 598, 628, 650), and the unique-key views iterate only request.project.check_set (hc/api/views.py:493, 684), giving 403 or 404. A checked-and-safe statement, NOT REAL as a defect claim.

True but not a defect: get_check passes readonly=request.readonly (hc/api/views.py:486), and to_dict with readonly omits uuid, ping_url, update_url, pause_url, resume_url and channels (hc/api/models.py:471-483). Safe-path statement, NOT REAL as a defect claim.

get_check_by_unique_key is @authorize_read (hc/api/views.py:491) and returns check.to_dict(v=request.v) without readonly (hc/api/views.py:495), so a read-only key gets uuid, ping_url and update/pause/resume URLs (hc/api/models.py:473-482). Read-only listing exposes unique_key (hc/api/models.py:471-472), so the chain list -> lookup -> UUID works; the lookup is limited to request.project.check_set (hc/api/views.py:493); update_check uses @authorize (hc/api/views.py:499) so configuration stays protected; delete via UUID works because of P-2. Matches ground truth P-3.

True but not a defect: create_check builds Check(project=request.project) (hc/api/views.py:451) and _lookup filters Check.objects.filter(project=project) with the key's project (hc/api/views.py:300, called at 446). Safe-path statement.

True but not a defect: create_check, update_check, pause, resume, pings, ping_body and channels use @authorize (hc/api/views.py:438, 499, 546, 573, 595, 625, 473), which calls for_api_key(accept_rw=True, accept_ro=False) (hc/api/decorators.py:59); with accept_ro False the hcr_ branch is skipped and only api_key is compared (hc/accounts/models.py:409-419, 429-433), so read-only keys of both kinds yield None and 401 (hc/api/decorators.py:60-61). Safe-path statement.

delete_check is decorated with @authorize_read (hc/api/views.py:520), which accepts hashed and legacy read-only keys (hc/api/decorators.py:82; hc/accounts/models.py:415-426), and the body never checks request.readonly before check.rename_and_delete() and a 200 JsonResponse (hc/api/views.py:521-529); pings and flips cascade (hc/api/models.py:691, 1361). The read-only key is the one a /tv/ dashboard link carries (hc/accounts/models.py:522-527). Matches ground truth P-2.

True but not a defect: channels filters Channel.objects.filter(project=request.project) (hc/api/views.py:475) and badges iterates request.project.check_set and uses request.project.badge_key (hc/api/views.py:695-698). Safe-path statement.

A scope statement, not a defect claim. The description is accurate: notification_status keys on the notification UUID (hc/api/views.py:816-821), metrics on X-Metrics-Key (hc/api/views.py:855-861), bounces on a signed bounce id (hc/api/views.py:883-887), status is public (hc/api/views.py:873-878).

True but not a defect: for_api_key narrows candidates by the 8-char prefix (hc/accounts/models.py:410-418) and compare_api_key computes HMAC over the full key and uses hmac.compare_digest (hc/accounts/models.py:592-593), so a prefix collision only adds candidates. Safe-path statement.

True but not a defect: request.readonly = api_key.startswith('hcr_') or api_key == project.api_key_readonly (hc/api/decorators.py:87-89) is True for hashed hcr_ keys and legacy keys matching api_key_readonly, False for hcw_ keys (stored value is a hash, hc/accounts/models.py:556) and legacy rw keys. Safe-path statement.

True but not a defect: cors sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin * and allows only the X-Api-Key header, with no Allow-Credentials (hc/api/decorators.py:112-115), and authentication uses the header or body key, not cookies (hc/api/decorators.py:49-54, 74-77). Safe-path statement.

The factual parts hold: create_check reads num_checks_available (hc/api/views.py:448; count at hc/accounts/models.py:342) and saves later in _update (hc/api/views.py:401) with no lock; the web UI does the same (hc/front/views.py:531); over_limit_date is never assigned in code, only shown in admin (hc/accounts/admin.py:137). But the claim leaves defect status open, and the code treats the plan limit as a soft account quota (auto-provisioning allows 2x the limit, hc/api/views.py:273): a bounded overshoot by the holder of that account's own read-write key crosses no access boundary. Not graded as a defect.

The documented example response for list flips is a bare JSON array (templates/docs/api.md:1417-1430), while flips() returns JsonResponse({'flips': [...]}) (hc/api/views.py:669) and the tests read doc['flips'] (hc/api/tests/test_get_flips.py:41). A real documentation defect, not a security one; outside the ground truth.

The quoted wording exists (templates/docs/api.md:94, 1170; templates/docs/apiv2.md:102, 1100; templates/docs/apiv1.md:82, 1070), but the same page states that all API keys are project-specific (templates/docs/api.md:49). 'The user' there is loose shorthand for the API caller and describes no concrete behaviour wrongly, so this is an editorial suggestion rather than a defect.

The Response Codes list for the ping body endpoint gives 200, 403, 404 and 503 with no 401 (templates/docs/api.md:1326-1338), and its 403 entry says 'wrong API key' (templates/docs/api.md:1331-1332). ping_body is @authorize (hc/api/views.py:625), which returns 401 for a missing, wrong or read-only key (hc/api/decorators.py:56-61). A real documentation defect; outside the ground truth.

A not-a-problem statement: the 403 vs 404 split exists (hc/api/views.py:482-484), is documented as 403 (templates/docs/api.md:1183), and check codes default to uuid4 (hc/api/models.py:196). NOT REAL as a defect claim.

A not-a-problem statement: ping_body returns one ping of a check in the key's project (hc/api/views.py:627-629, 636) and rejects n at or below n_pings - ping_log_limit (hc/api/views.py:631-634); the 1000 cap applies to the list (hc/api/views.py:606). NOT REAL as a defect claim.

True that [A-z0-9]{40} (hc/api/urls.py:21) also admits [ \ ] ^ _ and backtick, but the value is only compared with the hex SHA-1 unique_key of the key's own project's checks (hc/api/models.py:432-434; hc/api/views.py:493-494, 684-685). Harmless, as the claim says; NOT REAL as a defect claim.

A not-exploitable statement: the legacy lookup is a DB equality (hc/accounts/models.py:426, 431, 436), hashed keys use compare_digest (hc/accounts/models.py:593); the claim concludes no defect. NOT REAL as a defect claim.

True but not a defect: compare_api_key picks api_key_readonly for hcr_ keys and api_key otherwise (hc/accounts/models.py:582-585), consistent with the prefix-specific candidate queries (hc/accounts/models.py:409-418). Safe-path statement.

(hc/accounts/models.py:588-589). Safe-path statement.

True but not a defect: _update resolves '*' and named or coded channels only from Channel.objects.filter(project=check.project) (hc/api/views.py:323, 330, 336). Safe-path statement.

A no-failure statement, not a defect claim: update_check catches Check.NotUpdated (hc/api/views.py:514) with Django[argon2]==6.1.1 pinned (requirements.txt:3); Model.NotUpdated is a Django 6.0+ model exception (from knowledge of Django, not verifiable in the checkout). NOT REAL as a defect claim.

A scope statement, not a defect claim. Ping, slug ping and badge endpoints are not API-key protected (hc/api/views.py:729-742, 783-789; hc/api/urls.py:75-97), and the dashboard link is hc/accounts/models.py:522-527.
A scope statement about web UI key management (hc/accounts/views.py:385-407), not a defect claim.

notes: Ground truth used as written for P-1 (hc/api/views.py:415), P-2 (hc/api/views.py:520) and P-3 (hc/api/views.py:495); the code at those lines matches the described mechanisms.

Claims that only state a path was checked and found safe, or that scope was not examined, are graded NOT REAL as defect claims even where the statement is accurate (A-2, A-3, A-5, A-6, A-8 to A-12, A-17 to A-27).

in_zone: claims about Project.for_api_key / compare_api_key in hc/accounts/models.py (A-10, A-20, A-21) are marked 'no' because that code is outside the three zone files, though hc/api/decorators.py calls it. Non-API-key endpoints (A-9), capability URLs (A-26), web UI key management (A-27) and docs under templates/docs (A-14, A-15, A-16) are marked 'no'.

A-13 (check-limit race) is borderline: the race exists, but the claim leaves defect status open and the code treats the limit as a soft quota (2x tolerance at hc/api/views.py:273), with no access boundary crossed. Graded NOT REAL; a stricter reading would make it a low-severity REAL outside GT.

A-14 and A-16 are graded REAL as documentation defects (concrete mismatches between documented responses and code), outside GT and outside the zone. A-15 is graded NOT REAL as loose wording that misstates no concrete behaviour.

A-16 location: an omission sits on no single line. templates/docs/api.md:1331 is the 403 entry the missing 401 would precede, within the Response Codes list 1326-1338, and its text ('wrong API key') is itself the case the code answers with 401, so both location readings are 'yes'.

A-7: the dashboard parenthetical is supported by Project.dashboard_url (hc/accounts/models.py:522-527), which puts api_key_readonly in the /tv/ fragment; no template links it, but this does not affect the P-2 mechanism.
A-25: the existence of Model.NotUpdated in Django 6.1.1 comes from knowledge of Django, not from the checkout. It does not affect the verdict because the claim asserts no defect.
